content: 1. In 2021, Sysmex Asia Pacific highlighted advancements in hepatitis C screening and care. 2. Snelgrove CA, in 2018, introduced a quality improvement initiative aimed at standardizing hepatitis C screening as a routine part of medical care. 3. Shen NT and colleagues, in 2018, examined the effects of state-mandated hepatitis C virus (HCV) screening laws and automated confirmatory testing on reducing healthcare disparities across medical and surgical departments. 4. Seña AC and collaborators, in 2016, implemented a hepatitis C testing and linkage-to-care program at the local public health level, emphasizing frontline efforts. 5. Seaman A and team, in 2021, developed a hepatitis C elimination model for healthcare services targeting homeless populations, incorporating a novel reflexive laboratory algorithm and equity assessments. 6. Schechter-Perkins EM and colleagues, in 2018, reported on the implementation and preliminary outcomes of a non-targeted, opt-out hepatitis C screening program in an emergency department setting. 7. Saludes V and collaborators, in 2020, evaluated the Xpert HCV VL Fingerstick point-of-care assay and dried blood spot HCV-RNA testing as simplified diagnostic strategies for people who inject drugs in Catalonia, Spain. 8. Rhea S and team, in 2018, integrated hepatitis C testing and linkage-to-care services within a sexually transmitted disease clinic at a local health department, identifying essential resources and evaluating outcomes. 9. Ramachandran B and colleagues, in 2019, launched the HEAD-START project in Manipur, India, focusing on community-centric HCV testing and treatment for people who inject drugs. 10. Qureshi H and collaborators, in 2017, documented a partnership between a civil society organization and private gastroenterologists to diagnose and treat hepatitis C patients in Pakistan. 11. Piazzolla AV and team, in 2021, identified a high prevalence of undiagnosed hepatitis C infections among hospitalized patients aged 55–85 in Italy. 12. Park JS and colleagues, in 2021, conducted a retrospective review of hepatitis C screening among high-risk patients in a community hospital emergency department, analyzing patient characteristics and future implications. 13. Munang M and collaborators, in 2019, assessed the outcomes and costs of single-step hepatitis C testing in primary care settings in Birmingham, United Kingdom. 14. Mohamed Z and team, in 2020, demonstrated that point-of-care screening and streamlined linkage-to-care significantly improved hepatitis C treatment uptake among prisoners in England. 15. Martínez-Campreciós J and colleagues, in 2021, showed that reflex viral load testing using dried blood spots generated by plasma separation cards enabled effective screening and diagnosis of chronic viral hepatitis. 16. López-Martínez R and collaborators, in 2019, reported significant improvements in hepatitis C diagnosis using a one-step strategy in a central laboratory, suggesting its potential as an optimal tool for hepatitis C elimination. 17. Llerena S and team, in 2020, extended hepatitis C micro-elimination efforts beyond prison walls by screening and providing immediate assisted treatment to individuals with non-custodial sentences, supported by navigators and telemedicine. 18. Lens S and colleagues, in 2020, described an externalized HCV linkage-to-care cascade at Barcelona’s largest harm reduction center, targeting high-risk populations who inject drugs. 19. Lee AB and collaborators, in 2020, evaluated the burden of hepatitis C and the effectiveness of screening among high-risk populations in Alabama. 20. Lazarus J and team, in 2020, introduced a novel hepatitis C intervention in Denmark to test and treat people who inject drugs. 21. Cleland CM and colleagues, in 2020, analyzed hepatitis C care continuum outcomes and community viral loads among patients in an opioid treatment program. 22. Jonas MC and collaborators, in 2016, streamlined the hepatitis C cascade of care at Kaiser Permanente Mid-Atlantic States, improving screening-to-treatment processes. 23. Japaridze M and team, in 2020, decentralized hepatitis C testing to harm reduction sites in Georgia as part of the HEAD-START initiative. 24. Huang CF and colleagues, in 2021, scaled up the in-hospital hepatitis C care cascade in Taiwan, demonstrating improved outcomes. 25. Howes N and collaborators, in 2016, developed clinical care pathways to address critical barriers to effective hepatitis C treatment. 26. Hirsch AA and team, in 2014, implemented and evaluated a multi-component quality improvement intervention to enhance the efficiency of hepatitis C screening and diagnosis. 27. Hellard M, in 2020, conducted community-based point-of-care hepatitis C testing and initiated direct-acting antiviral therapy through general practitioners in Yangon, Myanmar. 28. Hamid S and colleagues, in 2021, identified the lower age limit for hepatitis C screening in large elimination programs in highly endemic areas. 29. The London Joint Working Group on Substance Use and Hepatitis C, in 2020, contributed to hepatitis C elimination efforts. 30. Ford JS and collaborators, in 2021, implemented universal hepatitis C screening in emergency departments using a best practice advisory system. 31. Coyle C and team, in 2016, integrated routine HCV testing into primary care at five federally qualified health centers in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, and shared lessons learned. 32. Chang TS and colleagues, in 2021, conducted village-to-village hepatitis B and C screening in remote communities using quantitative HBsAg and anti-HCV testing with reflex HCV core antigen tests. 33. Casas P and collaborators, in 2019, piloted reflex testing for active hepatitis C diagnosis at two healthcare centers. 34. Casas MP and team, in 2020, implemented reflex testing in Andalusia as part of efforts to eliminate hepatitis C. 35. Calner P and collaborators, in 2019, analyzed hepatitis C screening, linkage-to-care, and treatment patterns across various sites within an academic medical center. 36. Butsashvili M and team, in 2019, integrated hepatitis C treatment with harm reduction services in Georgia, presenting preliminary findings. 37. Bielen R and colleagues, in 2019, evaluated hepatitis C screening in emergency departments in Belgium, questioning whether baby boomers should also be screened. 38. Averhoff F and collaborators, in 2020, reviewed the progress and challenges of Georgia’s pioneering hepatitis C elimination program. 39. Patel RC and team, in 2016, reported on the outcomes of hepatitis C birth-cohort testing and linkage-to-care at selected U.S. sites. 40. Mera J and collaborators, in 2016, identified and managed individuals with chronic hepatitis C infection in the Cherokee Nation. 41. Janjua NZ and team, in 2016, described the population-level cascade of care for hepatitis C in British Columbia, Canada, using the BC Hepatitis Testers Cohort. 42. Ndagijimana A and colleagues, in 2015, evaluated one-stop TB-HIV services in Rwanda, comparing cohorts from 2001–2005 and 2006–2010. 43. Gamell A and team, in 2017, implemented the Option B+ cascade for preventing mother-to-child HIV transmission in rural Tanzania using a one-stop clinic model.
